en: The Heart Dharani for Making the World a House of Water:
Tadyathā | Ja-lam-ba | Mahā-ja-lam-ba | Anu-ha-ja-lam-ba | Sa-ra-ja-lam-ba | U-ga-ja-lam-ba | Yakṣa-vīra-ja-lam-ba.
Vana-ga-jalamba-uraga-viraja-jalamba-asati-biri-jalamba-aśva-pi-biri-jalamba-matsya-pi-biri-jalamba-manduka-pi-biri-jalamba-kakuda-pi-biri-jalamba.
Bhaṅgi-biri-ja-lamba-ama-biri-ja-lamba | Su-jhi-mukha-ja-lamba | Bha-ma-ra bha-ma-ra-ja-lamba | Ma-ra-bi-ja-ka-ta-pa-tra-pu-sphu-pa-pha-la-mba | Su-kha-ri-go-pa-su-dha-ma-ya-ja ||
Biliḥ, ciḥ, sāhilibāgā, stambhura, bhoṅ, bhorabhoṅ, bindubhoṅ, bharaja-bhi, svāhā. This dharani-phrase:
if one recites it for the sake of another person or for one's own body while calling their name, [it shall bring about protection].
This dhāraṇī completely extinguishes all fears and all calamities.
It is the Water-Wind Maṇi-Palace Dhāraṇī-Cakra.
Tadyathā: subhara, varati, nanavarati, che (level tone).
Ṣaṭaparānti | Anaparānti | Śabdaghora-parānti | Śaraṇaparānti | Kumuniparānti | Sañjīraparānti | Cidatasaraparānti | Saraparānti | Sara ||
Parihari sarabharata parihari nana parihari pīvikā parihariyañña parihari subhara parihari bindu parihari jarā parihari khettara.
Parihari, takṣaparihari, sannimāparihari, supoṣapratiri,
kumāramada-sokhi, anaya-palūśi, milābhami, arana-kauśi-kharaviśave, nara.
Yan-na-bi-shen-lin-bei, You-luo-jia-a-ni-mi-sha,
Gong-sha-luo-po-hu-mi-he-sha-zhai-bei, Jie-mo-pi-luo-li,
She-luo-mo-na-sa-li-li-ke-he-luo-jia-xie-mi, A-si-na-mi, A-qi-ni-bo-di-li, Neng.
Kauṇḍilya-pārāyaṇa-kāraṇī, Gandhāra-vṛji-śakrasya ye,
Anāthapiṇḍada-tīrtha-naya-nandili-tīrthe-dhūpa-buddha-ākhyāte svāhā! May this be for the sake of the devaputra of this land.
And may their retinues all be auspicious. *Svāhā*. *Nārāyaṇa nile svāhā*. *Cakrāve cakrāme svāhā*.
By the power of this dhāraṇī, one can eliminate all strife, all poisonous harms, and [the threats of] yakṣas, rākṣasas, and asuras.
All calamities caused by rākṣasas, dragons, humans, non-humans, and other such beings, as well as by birds and beasts— namely, untimely winds,
heat, cold, disaster clouds, droughts, and floods— are all completely extinguished.
This dhāraṇī is able to cause the five grains to all ripen excellently,
and to increase the lifespan, physical radiance, livelihood, peace and happiness, freedom from affliction, renown, observance of precepts,
extensive learning, generosity, loving-kindness, compassion, wisdom, skillful means, samādhi, and dhāraṇīs for all sentient beings.
The bhikṣuṇī contemplates the joy of transcending the world, transforming sentient beings, and entering the Mahāyāna.

She progresses through the stages of supreme vows, observing the aggregates and elements, and practicing shame and remorse. She gathers the merits for adorning the Buddha-lands and practices the six pāramitās.
She is constantly protected and remembered by all Buddhas of the ten directions; she has encountered and passed beyond [all obstacles].
The Buddha is the good friend of all bodhisattvas; through his playful mastery of supernatural powers (*ṛddhi*), he destroys all afflictions so that they do not increase,

and by means of his supernormal faculties (*abhijñā*), he enables them to cross to the other shore so that all wholesome qualities (*kuśala-dharma*)— up to and including unsurpassed *nirvāṇa*— do not decline.
The Great Dhāraṇī of the Power of Grinding. Tadyathā:
nabi mahānabi cūharanavi abhikunavi saṃśusananavi biharājakhavi āpa.
Lomuni | Dharuṇahuhe | Natabhatele | Japatume | Marasade | Temirabhatele | Kṣaṇḍa | Nirlehale | Cakṣubhasi | Khaṇḍavimekhi | Tidiye | Svāhā ||
Svāhā | Aṅgurākṣi svāhā | Bhusuṇḍyame svāhā | Parṣave svāhā | Sacittadūṣe svāhā | Śarīra-nābhakārama-viśa svāhā | This dhāraṇī.
Nigu protects the king. Svāhā!
By the power of this dhāraṇī, may all that is required for the fruit and retribution of all beings, as well as the essence of the earth, never diminish;
may none be able to destroy or seize it. May the vital energy of the earth not be released as poisonous gas, and may its excellent flavor remain unimpaired, capable of producing the five [senses].
The grains and medicinal herbs do not have their vital essence usurped; they are free from toxic vapors, do not wither or dry up, and are neither astringent nor foul.
They do not fail to ripen, and they are not harmed by cold or heat. Their consumption is unimpeded, and once eaten, they are non-toxic. (A brief excerpt.)
The Bodhisattva Nāgarāja Sumerugarbha spoke this mantra:
*Tadyathā | sadambavuja | viliṭabuja | śukulubliṭabuja | meruja-paga-cuvabuja | yam-yam*.
Anivāsaja, sumarābaddhavāsaja, svabhūvāsaja svāhā.
This dharani mantra phrase protects [the name of] so-and-so, svāhā.
If there are sentient beings who are afflicted and disturbed by various venomous dragons, they should invoke my name and recite this dharani.
"O Āraṇi, I shall extinguish this dragon's greedy, hateful, arrogant, envious, poisonous, and evil mind;
I cannot allow it to produce untimely winds, rains, cold, heat, droughts, floods, calamities, hail, or evils."
This Nāga King Supratiṣṭhita is the lord of all elephant nāgas;
these Nanda and Upananda Nāga Kings are the lords of all serpent nāgas; this Anavatapta Nāga King is the lord of all horse nāgas;
this Varuṇa Nāga King is the lord of all fish nāgas; this Mānasvin...
The Imperial Dragon King is the lord of all frogs and dragons.
The Dragon King Sthira speaks this mantra: *Tadyathā | nāgāṃbuṣṭhe | nāganime | nāgadha*.
Rauśkara śukara jala-śukara abhimarji svāhā saramukhi karate pucche yavasattvaṃ vidi-jaye bappiṅge vimuśakre svāhā.
Thus, by these dharani-words, may [so-and-so] be protected, and may all fears and all calamities be entirely extinguished. Svāhā.
The Dragon King Nanda and the Dragon King Upananda spoke this mantra:
Tadyathā | Paranasyume | Kūṇapadhūrakīvaruṇakubje | Agarakī | Ciśanivimāharaṅgakī | Kūṇabhirārage | Atosale | Nayanaḍambhe | Karakuśe ||
Śyāma, Bhīma, Pāra, Jambha, Kāṇḍa, Hiraṇyabāhu, Svāhā!
By these dhāraṇī phrases, may [the name of] such-and-such person be protected, svāhā!
The Nāga King Anavatapta spoke this mantra:
Tadyathā | Namaḥ piliśe | Nabaye ma-piliśe | Anucana-pakung-uśa-ni-ki | Khaga-pe-kha-pratolū-aṭṭe-haśas-re | Naraśana-gumi | Vina-sit-tre | A ||
Sakārame acūṣṇiye śe munisatve svāhā.
By this dhāraṇī, may [Name] be protected and freed from fear and calamity, svāhā.
Then the Nāga King Varuṇa spoke this mantra:
Tadyathā | kṣemavati | parakiṇa gune | dantapindatīriṇi | vārakṣadali me | gaṅgukumi | viśamugmi śe | turumute mahe | dantakūse | jhamakhike ||
Cāra-hara-aṅgīna-ta-daḍi | Gandaka-gatule | Svāhā | This dharani-phrase protects [Name]. Svāhā.
The Naga King Manasvapati spoke this mantra:
Dhṛti-dhare dharaṇi-dhare buddha-kṣaye vara-kṣaye amani-mati-buddha-sari-ri āva-mite prātihārya-nirdeśe āvani-lame khira-śūre nāsu-dupe paribhāṣe śānte svāhā.
Gandhāri parāṇakṣaye svāhā. This dhāraṇī protects [the name of] such-and-such person, svāhā.
When the Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha was about to speak the Great Dhāraṇī Gate of the Banner Staff, all those who heard it but once with their ears—
All illnesses shall be completely cured, and all afflictions such as greed, hatred, and delusion shall likewise be eliminated;

even if they are not entirely extinguished, they shall be rendered light and thin. Furthermore, one shall attain pure faith in the Buddha-dharma, and in future lives, one’s livelihood shall be abundant and one shall be beloved by all people. Then he spoke the mantra:
Tadyathā | Bhaṅgapā | Madī alupa | Madī kīdrābupakṣaṇḍi | Kūṇama-kriye | Maccanule | Kāharaṇadi | Nakṣabhami bhaṇḍa-arasumī | Bhagala-kiḷime ||
Rohitāśvā nāgarājñī svāhā | bhagana-ikṣiṇi antaja-āvartaka-rāvaśe kṣetra-rohi samādhitopale svāhā | By these dhāraṇī phrases,
may [Name] be protected and freed from all fear. Svāhā.
Pāṭha!

This *Mahāvidyārājñī*, the Great Dhāraṇī of the Eye of the Vow of the Maṇi Banner-Top, spoken by the Bodhisattva Akṣayamati, which articulates the speech of all Tathāgatas, possesses great majesty, great power, and great might; it fulfills extensive learning.
This treasury is filled with the treasury of wisdom, accomplished by all Buddhas and Śrāvakas. If there is anyone who, for as long as life lasts,
dwells in pure precepts, dwells in the Upāsaka precepts, dwells in the Śrāmaṇera precepts, or dwells in the full ordination (Upasaṃpadā) precepts—
whether they be a worthy vessel or not— who is able to receive this Mahādhāraṇī of the Great Vow-Eye of the Banner and Parasol Maṇi;

If one maintains, reads, and recites this for seven days and seven nights, employing the skillful means of wise observation to constantly contemplate the five aggregates of clinging (*pañca-upādāna-skandha*),
and repeatedly recites this great *dhāraṇī* for a full hundred thousand times during those seven days and seven nights, one will immediately attain the power of hearing and retaining (*śruta-dhara*).
Upon hearing it, one will be able to receive and uphold it, and will gain immeasurable eloquence (*pratibhāna*), thereby enabling [the conversion of] Kṣatriyas, Brāhmaṇas, Vaiśyas, and so forth.

Śūdras and all sentient beings shall give rise to reverent faith; furthermore, they shall be made abundant in wealth and property, proceed toward the heavenly realms, and always attain proximity to the Buddhas. He then spoke the mantra:
Tadyathā | Tinduka | Sañjaya-ke | Binduka | Vinika-lam-dha-ca | Pūvasuve | Cāmara-cchavi-aparaca-acala-rupe | Acala-dumati-mili-siri-bhavi-sava ||
Liyāṅqúshātúoshìní shāsháluónúmí ānàmóshūdimílīqi qīlīchā nílúpóqì wèiqiápōchā pàopóshāpólìhéfúlì dìsūbù shāpólúqíshì sùmódì.
Muni svāhā. This dhāraṇī protects [the name of] such-and-such person, svāhā.

Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva desires that all trees, flowers, fruits, the five grains, medicinal flavors, sprouts, stalks, branches, leaves, and the requisites for the sustenance of sentient beings dwelling upon the earth throughout these four continents be made abundant and sufficient. Svāhā.
For the sake of protection, I shall proclaim this Great Dhāraṇī named "Able-to-Frighten Śiri-Śirinu.

Within these four continents, it is rare and unprecedented; it causes all seeds, sprouts, stalks, branches, leaves, flowers, fruits, medicinal tastes, moisture, and sweet flavors to increase and become entirely abundant.
It enables all sentient beings to practice faith, precepts, and extensive learning.
Bestowing wisdom, compassion, and skillful means to nurture all factors conducive to enlightenment (bodhipākṣika-dharma),
he then spoke this mantra before the Buddha:
*Tadyathā | amanye jvati | gava kha viśi ku lu ca lu*.
Mī śrī-śākya-jusumina-ba-ju-mun-di (dù-mài qiè) hé-luó-shā-ba-mī-chē-zhà-bō-bō-mo-zè-bì-sù-hěn-qí-ā-fó-luó-sù-lì-hé-sā-gā-shā-chā lú-mó-fú-shā-chā qián-pí-luó-bō-sù-mī ā-nú-mó-shé.
*Sariprasādudaye svāhā*. This dhāraṇī phrase protects [the name of] such-and-such person, *svāhā*.
Having written this dhāraṇī upon a high banner, one should praise and recite it with a loud voice; furthermore, by means of this...
Recite this dhāraṇī mantra one thousand times over the juice of the *ana* fruit and scatter it upon trees, field crops, and the five grains. Alternatively,
if one consecrates various conch shells or drums with this mantra and blows them, then wherever the sound reaches,
all flowers, fruits, five grains, medicinal herbs, and flavors growing from the earth shall be incapable of being destroyed by any calamity.
[It] can dry up [all afflictions], and so forth.
The Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara spoke this Great Dhāraṇī of the Merit of the Ship Flower:
*tadyathā | lambu-sāphalika-sāyabame | sacemipā*.
Kle dha-bha-he-laṅkā-jale mūli-ca-su-he-cha-svabhāri-su-ha-vāyu-gī-aparokā-dhale-siddha-he-vihe-vibhaca-che-he-na-pinva-he-ri abhiśānta-ātve sāpa-cara-a.
Varāhasya varāhacūḍe | likhaka haradūte | samādhi-karṇi-vara-jñānate | mahā-buddha-kośe | araṇa-nile | varāha-same | nīla-kusume | svāhā ||
This dharani-phrase protects the sovereign of the land; svāhā!

If any sentient beings hear the sound of this dharani even once, reaching their ears—even down to the most minute mosquitoes, gnats, and insects—all turbid and evil thoughts will be completely extinguished, and they shall attain a mind that dwells securely within wholesome dharmas; how much more so for others?

If people hear this dhāraṇī, and if there is anyone who desires rain, they should go to a spring source or a place where dragons dwell and recite this dhāraṇī one thousand and eight times each day for seven days.
Furthermore, they should scatter various beautiful flowers, famous incenses, and food of a hundred flavors into the dragon pond. Only...
Abstaining from alcohol, meat, the five pungent roots, and impure foods, from the seventh day of the month until the fourteenth,
one should on the morning of the fifteenth mix powdered black pepper with sesame oil and recite the mantra over it one thousand and eight times.
Smearing this upon a white cotton cloth and casting it into a dragon spring will cause that dragon to feel great joy toward that person and immediately pour down heavy rain.
The World-Honored One then spoke in verse:
"All sufferings that arise Are caused by food and drink; If one is free from food and drink, No sufferings will arise."
The Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara spoke the mantra, saying:
*Tadyathā | munivīra | munināka | munipara | munisari | saṃdhāvaprasādite kṣatraparānate* ||
Vaya vaya sarva viśa vaya siri ri svāhā.
This dhāraṇī phrase protects [Name] svāhā. Phonetic glosses:
*ti* (the hair of the head); *dhu* (pronounced as in *ding-dou*); *pi* (same as *bi*, the thigh).
